To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) children with a low IQ are generally perceived by their preschool teachers as having few problems in terms of social integration in the daycare setting; (2) attachment security is not a good predictor of social integration for children with intellectual deficiencies, but the Q Sort procedure may not be an adequate measure of attachment for children in the low IQ group; and (3) children with a high IQ are generally perceived as having fewer problems in social integration than children with a low or average IQ.
the low IQ children are generally perceived by their preschool teachers as being socially well integrated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the social integration process of young children who are socio culturally retarded.
the social integration of preschool children who are socio culturally retarded.
the social integration of preschool children with intellectual deficiencies, as well as their mothers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a need to further explore the role of attachment in the development of social competence in preschoolers with intellectual deficiencies.
the social integration of cultural familial retarded preschoolers into the daycare setting is not a problem, but rather an achievement.
the results of this investigation indicate that children with mild to moderate mental retardation are able to integrate socially with their peers in a preschool setting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that children with intellectual deficiencies are able to develop social relationships with adults other than their mothers, and that the development of social relationships with adults in the daycare setting is not related to IQ.

we have been able to show that children who have been exposed to the risk of maltreatment are more likely to have a disorganized/disoriented pattern of attachment to their mothers than children who have not been exposed to the risks of maltreatment.

the socialization and integration of children with cultural familial deficiencies is a complex process that involves the child's cognitive abilities, the quality of the attachment to mother and the quality of the daycare environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the Attachment Q Sort with this population of preschoolers is questionable.

the social integration of preschool children with cultural familial intellectual deficiencies can be predicted as a function of their security of attachment with their mother, even though the quality of attachment is not necessarily related to their cognitive functioning.
the socialization of children with intellectual disabilities is not a linear process.
